title: From Manual Web Research to Automated Presentations
subtitle: Browser automation + AI analysis + report generation
problem: Producing a research presentation meant visiting many pages, reading, screenshotting, cropping, and writing slides by hand. Every report took hours and each person did it slightly differently.
oldProcess: Copy relevant information into a document
Take and crop screenshots one by one
Write analysis and paste everything into slides
Repeat from scratch for the next report
opportunity: Almost every step was deterministic except the analysis — and the analysis could be handled by an LLM if given clean, structured input and a fixed output schema.
system: A pipeline where Playwright drives the browser and captures pages and screenshots, an image-processing step crops and normalises the visuals, the LLM analyses the extracted content section by section with JSON-schema outputs, and a generator assembles a PowerPoint deck from a template. A reviewer approves before delivery.
result: Workflow implemented end to end: URL list → reviewed PPTX
Automation achieved for navigation, capture, cropping, analysis and slide assembly
Consistent report structure on every run
Human review retained as the final step
learned: Invest in resilient selectors and explicit waits before anything else
Schema-constrained LLM output is what makes automation safe to template
Screenshots are evidence — keep them alongside AI commentary

title: Repeatable SEO Research & Analysis
subtitle: Rule-based checks explained by AI, backed by screenshots
problem: SEO analysis for each site followed the same structure — technical checks, competitor comparison, keyword research — yet was performed manually every time.
oldProcess: Manually inspect pages for technical issues
Visit competitor sites and note differences
opportunity: Technical checks are rules. Competitor comparison is extraction. Keyword research is organisation. Only the narrative needs language — and that's exactly what an LLM is good at.
system: A browser crawler collects pages from the target and competitors, a checks module applies technical rules, a keyword workflow organises inputs for human decisions, and an LLM layer writes a prioritised narrative from the structured findings. Output is a report with an evidence appendix of screenshots. The system clearly presents findings — it does not promise ranking outcomes.
result: Workflow implemented: site + competitors → structured analysis report
Automation achieved for crawling, checks, evidence capture and report drafting
Keyword decisions kept with the human specialist
learned: Separate facts (rules) from interpretation (LLM) to keep reports trustworthy
Always label research systems honestly — no ranking guarantees
